author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell argues that control doesn’t always require force. He describes how information, interactions, and even chance encounters could be shaped to steer people toward certain outcomes.

He then says that even opposing political sides can remain trapped inside the same cultural framework — if the system defines the debate, it can still shape how people think.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to the idea of taxing AI and robots when they replace human labor, before pushing back on the broader pattern of billionaires offering solutions to problems created by increasingly centralized systems.

He then argues that AI could be used in a completely different way — to support self-governing, decentralized communities where people decide how their own resources are used. Russell contrasts that vision with digital ID, facial recognition and centralized control, saying the same technology could instead be redirected toward greater freedom.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Dr. Stella Immanuel tells Russell why she says her views on childhood vaccination changed, and why she would no longer take or administer another shot without stronger evidence of its benefits.

She also raises concerns about autism, ADHD, SIDS and chronic illness, explaining how those observations led her to question assumptions she once held as a pediatrician.
